query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for high-temperature and irradiation-exposed applications, what intervention could improve mechanical performance while maintaining thermal and irradiation stability? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a uniform dispersion of nanoscale Y₂O₃ particles in an equimolar W–Mo–Ta–Nb–V refractory high-entropy alloy will enhance its yield strength and reduce irradiation-induced swelling at 800 °C without compromising thermal stability.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar W₃₀Mo₃₀Ta₃₀Nb₁₀V₁₀ HEA produced by arc melting and homogenized at 1200 °C, with an average grain size of ~50 µm.
generation.intervention: Addition of 0.5 wt% Y₂O₃ nanoparticles via mechanical alloying followed by hot isostatic pressing to distribute ~10 nm dispersoids uniformly in the matrix.
generation.conditions: Mechanical testing at 800 °C in vacuum; irradiation with 3 MeV Ni²⁺ ions to 1 dpa at 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Stable Y₂O₃ dispersoids (~10 nm) located on grain boundaries and within grains.
generation.mechanism: Orowan strengthening by oxide particles impeding dislocation motion; oxide sites trap helium and self-interstitials, reducing void nucleation and growth under irradiation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength increase of ~30% at 800 °C relative to the undispersed HEA; irradiation-induced swelling reduced by ~50% after 1 dpa.
generation.baseline: Same HEA without Y₂O₃ under identical thermal and irradiation conditions.
generation.boundary: Effective for irradiation doses up to 5 dpa and temperatures between 700–900 °C; above 900 °C, coarsening of dispersoids may diminish strengthening.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; oxide stability under sustained high-flux irradiation in refractory HEAs has not been fully established.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys (with and without 0.5 wt% Y₂O₃). Verify dispersoid size/distribution by TEM. Measure tensile yield strength at 800 °C in vacuum. Irradiate both to 1 dpa with 3 MeV Ni²⁺ at 800 °C. Quantify swelling by TEM and density measurements.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Y₂O₃-containing HEA fails to show at least a 10% increase in yield strength at 800 °C or fails to reduce swelling by ≥30% after 1 dpa, the hypothesis is falsified.
